AlterLingua works through its own keyboard, so you can write in WhatsApp and other apps without leaving them.

Android keeps every keyboard switched off until you allow it. You\'ll open Android\'s keyboard list and switch AlterLingua on. Android shows a general warning that keyboards can see what you type. The AlterLingua keyboard only reads your text when you tap Translate or the microphone; it never stores it and never sends a message for you.

Android calls this \"notification access\". You\'ll open a system screen and switch it on for AlterLingua; Android asks you to confirm. It only covers what Android shows in your notifications, and only if your notification settings show message text. Messages are translated, not stored.
If the switch is greyed out, Android is blocking apps installed outside the Play Store. Open AlterLingua\'s app info, tap the ⋮ menu, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.

When this is on, AlterLingua reads the text shown on screen in WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger or Signal while one of them is open — not photos, not voice notes, not anything you type, and only while a supported app is the one you\'re using. That text is sent to AlterLingua\'s translation service and shown back to you as a translation drawn under each message on screen; it is never saved, and nothing is shared with anyone else. This needs Android\'s Accessibility permission, which you grant separately after agreeing here. AlterLingua is a translation tool, not an accessibility tool for people with disabilities.

Every real conversation is counted: messages you translate or dictate, and messages and voice notes you receive. For each useful word in them, AlterLingua checks your Personal Language Map at that moment. A word that was not yet mastered counts as needing translation. Translation dependence for a week is those words divided by all words met that week, as a percentage. A week needs at least 20 words to be shown, and a trend needs two such weeks. Lessons, reading practice and pronunciation practice are not counted as conversations. Words become mastered through lessons and recall checks, so the figure falls as you truly learn, not because you translate less.

1. Tap Start and approve Android’s screen-capture question. Android shows a small indicator while AlterLingua listens. Whichever option Android offers, AlterLingua only hears the chosen apps’ sound and never records your screen.
2. Go back to the chat and play the voice note.
3. When it ends, tap the “Voice note captured” notification to read the transcript and the translation.

AlterLingua records only the sound that chat app plays, only until the voice note ends. The recording is sent securely to be understood and translated, then deleted. Your screen is not recorded, and nothing is sent to anyone.
